newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian court revives Timor asylum case.
newsitem.headline: Australian court revives Timor asylum case.

text.p: An Australian court on Friday revived the hopes of 1,370 East Timorese asylum-seekers, ordering that one man's claim for refugee status be reviewed.
In a test case, the federal court ruled against the decision of a refugee tribunal to reject asylum-seeker Jong Kim Koe's claim for refugee status on grounds he was a Portuguese citizen.
Jong was born in East Timor in 1973, when the territory was ruled by colonial power Portugal. Indonesia invaded the territory in 1975 and annexed it the following year.
Last year, Jong argued before the Refugee Review Tribunal he was not Portuguese, but it went ahead and declared him to be Portuguese because he was born under Lisbon's rule.
The tribunal's ruling disappointed all 1,370 asylum-seekers who, like Jong, have been living in Australia for up to seven years and consider it their home. Jong appealed.
Supporters of the East Timorese have warned they will stage a campaign of civil disobedience and hide the 1,370 people if they lose their asylum cases and face deportation to Indonesia.
On Friday, the federal court upheld that Jong was a dual citizen of Portugal and Indonesia, but it said this did not necessarily make him the responsibility of Portugal.
"The effectiveness of (Portuguese) protection has to be considered as a practical matter in light of all the circumstances," the court ruled.
It ordered the refugee tribunal to review the case.

"We believe this federal court decision opens the door for the humanitarian consideration for residency of the East Timorese people," said Baptist minister Martin Rielly, head of the East Timorese Asylum-Seeker Action campaign
"The question is how the government responds to this decision," Rielly said.
A spokesman for the government said it would consider appealing to the country's peak court, the High Court of Australia. Canberra has hinted that the asylum-seekers may be Portugal's responsibility.

Many of the East Timorese asylum-seekers, including Jong, arrived in Australia soon after the 1991 shootings in Dili, the territory's capital. Indonesian troops fired on protesters, killing at least 50 by official count.
Even if the tribunal again rejects the claims for refugee status in Australia, the asylum-seekers want the government to grant them a special visa on humanitarian grounds.
